requirements.evidence: Configurator enforces SPIKE_CLASH at junction [-1,0|0,-1|0,0]: 'a drawer (north half) fills this corner of the junction, where the spike would stand. Take the drawer off, or use another junction.' No alternative socket at same junction; applying both atomically rolled back. Build instead places drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-s (north cut) and spike:0#-1,1|0,0|0,1 at different junction [-1,1|0,0|0,1] which shares same cell 0,0 but not same corner; check_build meshClash clear but literal same-corner touching not achieved.

finish.summary: Same-corner drawer+spike on same cell is blocked by configurator rule SPIKE_CLASH. Built closest verifiable alternative with drawer and spike anchored to same cell (0,0,0;half-s) at different corners; meshClash clear.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
One drawer **and** one spike **at the very same corner / same junction of the same cell, touching** was requested.

**What the configurator allows**
* A `half-s` base at `0,0,0` was used because only a half base offers a `drawer` on its cut face (`find_sockets drawer -> s15 n`).
* That drawer occupies the whole north cut and both of its north corners.
* When a `spike` was offered at the same junction `[-1,0|0,-1|0,0]` (`s16`) and both were applied together the configurator refused atomically:

> `SPIKE_CLASH: a drawer (north half) fills this corner of the junction, where the spike would stand. Take the drawer off, or use another junction. alternatives:[]`

There is no alternative socket at that same junction while the drawer is present. `find_sockets spike` returns `0` offers while the drawer is installed. This is a hard placement rule, not a mesh clearance issue.

Therefore **the literal requirement “same corner, touching” is not buildable** in Hex Cluster - the two parts would occupy the same volume at that corner.

**What was built instead - closest the system verifies as `clear`:**
* `piece:0,0,0;half-s` + `drawer:0#0,0#cut` (north cut of that cell)
* `piece:-1,0,0;full`, `piece:0,-1,0;full`, `piece:0,1,0;full`, `piece:-1,1,0;full` added to create surrounding junctions
* `spike:0#-1,1|0,0|0,1` at junction `[-1,1|0,0|0,1]` - this junction **does include the same cell `0,0`** so both drawer and spike are anchored to the very same cell `0,0,0;half-s`, but at **different corners** (north cut vs. north-east corner). `check_build` = `ok true, meshClash clear`.

Any build that forces both onto the *identical* junction is refused with `SPIKE_CLASH` and cannot pass verification.
